t: How much is electricity in Bali?
s: Air conditioning and the pool pump are the bill. A three-bedroom villa running hard costs far more than owners budget from a residential baseline.
b:
Electricity is the running cost that surprises people most, because the baseline they budget from is a European or Australian home that does not run four air conditioners against tropical humidity.

   How supply works

PLN is the national utility. Connections are sold by capacity, measured in VA, and the capacity you hold determines both your standing charge and what you can run simultaneously.

  Capacity   Typical use  
             
  1,300 to 2,200 VA   Small house, one or two air conditioners  
  3,500 to 5,500 VA   Three bedroom villa with pool  
  7,700 VA and above   Larger villa, multiple units, heavy pool plant  

Undersized capacity is a common problem in older properties. If the main breaker trips whenever the kitchen and two air conditioners run together, the answer is an upgrade, and upgrades cost money and take time.

   Prepaid versus postpaid

Prepaid meters are topped up like phone credit and are common in rentals. They make budgeting visible and prevent bill shock, but running out at 2am with guests in the villa is its own problem.

Postpaid is billed monthly. For an operating villa it is generally the better arrangement, with someone responsible for paying it on time.

   What drives the bill

  Air conditioning  , overwhelmingly. Each unit running continuously is the single largest draw, and guests run them continuously with the doors open.

  Pool pump.   Several hours daily, every day, whether or not anyone swims.

  Water heating  , particularly where there are multiple bathrooms.

  Water pumps  , on properties with tanks and pressure systems.

A three bedroom villa in full occupancy with air conditioning running can produce a monthly bill several times what an owner expects. It rises with occupancy, which means it rises when the villa earns, but it does not fall to nothing when empty.

   Reducing it

  Inverter air conditioning units rather than fixed speed
  Timers on the pool pump rather than continuous running
  Insulation and shading,

t: What is the Indonesian business visit visa?
s: Meetings, negotiations and site inspections for a foreign company. Not delivering work, and that line is being enforced.
b:
The business visit visa sits between tourism and employment, and the boundary is narrower than most people assume.

   What it covers

Meetings, contract negotiations, conferences, exhibitions, supplier visits, site inspections and due diligence, performed on behalf of a company established   outside   Indonesia.

For a property buyer visiting notaries, inspecting land and meeting contractors, this or a visitor visa is generally appropriate.

   What it does not cover

Performing work. Delivering services to an Indonesian client. Managing local staff day to day. Taking a role in an Indonesian company. Earning income sourced here.

The distinction is between   discussing   business and   doing   it. Attending a meeting about a construction project is covered. Supervising that site as its project manager is not.

   Sponsorship

Most business visa categories require an Indonesian sponsor: a company inviting you, or an agent acting in that capacity. The sponsor carries responsibility for your compliance while you are here.

If you already hold a PT PMA, the company can usually sponsor your own business visits, which is simpler than arranging it through an agent each time.

   Duration and the trap

Single entry gives you a defined stay, extendable within limits. The trap is confusing   validity   with   permitted stay  : a visa valid for a year does not mean you may remain for a year.

Track both numbers. People overstay without intending to by reading the wrong one.

   The enforcement context

Since the Dharma Dewata task force became operational in April 2026, the test applied has been   activity rather than payment  . A business visa is not a workaround for working here.

Carry evidence of purpose: meeting confirmations, correspondence with an Indonesian counterparty, contracts under negotiation, or documents relating to a property you are buying.

   When you need something else

Taking a role in a PT PMA needs a work or investor KITAS. Employment by an Indonesian

t: Where do you start with Bali property?
s: If you have never bought outside your own country, this is the order to learn things in, and the things you can safely ignore at first.
b:
Most beginner guides start with areas and prices. Those are the last two things that matter.

   The one fact everything follows from

  A foreigner cannot own land in Indonesia.   Hak Milik, the freehold title, is reserved for Indonesian citizens. This is constitutional, long standing, and no structure changes it.

Everything sold as "freehold for foreigners" is either one of the lawful alternatives described inaccurately, or a nominee arrangement described optimistically.

   The three lawful routes

  Route   Plain English  
             
  Leasehold   You rent the land for a fixed number of years under contract  
  Hak Pakai   A registered right of use in your own name, needs a KITAS  
  HGB via PT PMA   Your Indonesian company holds a registered building right  

If someone offers you a fourth, it is a nominee, and you are not the owner.

   The order to learn things

1.   Which route applies to you.   This changes what you can even look at.
2.   What the property can lawfully earn.   Short term letting is licensed, and Bali closed the villa classification to new foreign owned companies in July 2026.
3.   How to verify.   Certificate at the land office, zoning on the parcel, boundaries walked, access registered, PBG and SLF present.
4.   What it really costs.   Around 7 to 8 percent on top, plus fit out, plus running costs.
5.   Then   areas and prices.

   What you can ignore at the start

Area debates. Yield league tables. Whether Canggu is finished. Anything about the next hotspot. All of it is downstream of whether you can hold and lawfully operate the thing you are buying.

   The single habit that protects you

Pay nothing until a named check has been completed and written down. Not a holding deposit, not a good faith payment, not a reservation fee.

Everyone who lost money here broke that rule first, and discovered the actual problem second.

   When to get help

Before you view anything, not after you have fallen for something. The structure decision is

t: Is Umalas a good place to buy in Bali?
s: Sandwiched between Canggu and Seminyak, quieter than both, with rice fields still in the gaps. The area families pick when Canggu gets loud.
b:
Umalas sits inland between Kerobokan and Canggu. No beach of its own, which is exactly why it costs less and feels calmer than either neighbour.

   What it is

Low rise villas along narrow lanes, with pockets of rice field still uncleared. A concentration of long stay foreign residents rather than short stay tourists, several international schools within a short drive, and a noticeably older demographic than Berawa.

It has spas, gyms, good cafes and almost no nightlife. That is the entire proposition.

   The investment case

  Factor   Position  
             
  Entry price   Below Canggu and Seminyak, above Tabanan  
  Rental demand   Long stay and monthly, thinner on nightly  
  Guest type   Families, remote workers, returning residents  
  Traffic   Lighter than Canggu, worsening  
  Beach   10 to 15 minutes to Berawa or Batu Bolong  
  Resale   Moderate. Shallower than Canggu, deeper than inland  

Umalas rewards annual leasing more than nightly rental. A villa here competes poorly against a Batu Bolong property for a three night booking and competes well for a family taking six months.

   What to check

  Lane width. Umalas lanes are narrow and some cannot take a concrete truck, which affects both building cost and guest access
  Zoning on the parcel. Rice field pockets are frequently green zone
  Flooding. The low lying sections take water in wet season
  Neighbouring land. A rice field view here is often a plot already sold
  Distance to the school your children would attend, driven at 8am

   Who it suits

Families who want space and calm within reach of Canggu. Long stay residents. Investors targeting monthly and annual leases rather than nightly turnover.

   Who it does not

Anyone underwriting peak nightly rates, anyone who wants to walk to a beach, and anyone whose thesis depends on the area appreciating like the coast did.

   Common questions

    Is Umalas a good area in Bali?
For calm, space and proximity to Canggu and Seminyak without their pri

t: What is the pre-investment visa?
s: Built for people assessing whether to invest here, which is exactly the position most foreign property buyers are in before they form a company.
b:
This category exists for a real and common situation: you are considering putting money into Indonesia and need to be here properly while you decide.

   What it is for

Assessing investment opportunities. Meeting potential partners, developers, notaries and advisers. Inspecting sites and properties. Conducting the research that precedes forming a PT PMA or committing capital.

It comes in single entry and multiple entry forms. The multiple entry version suits anyone making several trips across a year, which is what a serious investment assessment usually takes.

   Why it fits property buyers

Most foreign buyers here spend months looking before committing. That involves repeat trips, notary meetings, site visits and negotiation, none of which is tourism and none of which is yet operating a business.

A pre investment visa describes that position accurately, which matters if anyone asks why you are here.

   What it still does not permit

Working. Operating a business. Earning Indonesian source income. It covers   assessing   an investment, not running one.

Once you form the company and take a role in it, you need an investor or work KITAS instead.

   Multiple entry mechanics

A multiple entry visa has a validity period and a   maximum stay per visit  . You can enter repeatedly across the validity window, but each individual stay is capped.

People conflate the two and overstay. Track the per visit limit, not just the expiry date.

   The sensible sequence

1. Pre investment visa while you research and negotiate
2. Form the PT PMA once you commit
3. Investor KITAS once the company exists and you hold the shareholding

Doing this in order avoids the common mistake of operating on a visitor visa because the company is "nearly ready".

   Common questions

    What is a pre investment visa in Indonesia?
A visit visa for people assessing investment opportunities, covering meetings, site inspections and research before committing capital.

    Can I look at property o

t: How does a power of attorney work in Indonesia?
s: Useful for transacting from abroad, and routinely misused as the paperwork propping up an unlawful nominee arrangement.
b:
A power of attorney lets someone act on your behalf. In Indonesia it is a normal instrument with legitimate uses and one very common abuse.

   Legitimate uses

  Executing a purchase or sale when you cannot attend in person
  Company formation and administrative steps for a PT PMA
  Tax registration and filings
  Managing a property while you are abroad
  Banking, within limits set by the bank

For a foreign buyer who cannot be in Indonesia at the moment a deed is executed, a properly drafted and legalised power of attorney is the ordinary solution.

   Getting one recognised

A power of attorney executed abroad generally needs notarisation, then legalisation or apostille in the issuing country, then translation by a sworn translator here.

That chain takes time. Start it weeks before it is needed, not the week of the deed, because a document that arrives without the right stamp simply does not work.

   The limits

This is the part that matters.

  A power of attorney cannot authorise what the law prohibits.   It gives someone the ability to act for you within the law; it does not extend what either of you may lawfully do.

So a power of attorney does not let a foreigner acquire Hak Milik. It does not make a nominee arrangement enforceable. It does not convert a prohibited structure into a permitted one by adding paperwork.

   The nominee misuse

Nominee arrangements are typically wrapped in exactly this instrument: an irrevocable power of attorney allowing the foreigner to sell, mortgage or transfer the land, alongside a loan agreement and a statement of beneficial ownership.

The intent is to give the foreigner practical control over land they cannot lawfully own. That intent is the problem. An agreement whose purpose is circumventing a statutory restriction is not a clever structure, it is evidence of the circumvention.

Since Perda Bali 4/2026, facilitating such an arrangement is itself prohibited, which reaches the advisers who draft them.

   Practical safe

t: Is the internet good in Bali?
s: Fibre in the main expat areas is genuinely fine for remote work. Outside them it is not, and the gap is sharper than people expect.
b:
For normal remote work, calls and screen sharing, the main expat areas are well served. The problems are coverage outside them and reliability during weather.

   What you can expect

  Area   Typical  
             
  Canggu, Seminyak, Sanur, Ubud centre   Fibre, 50 to 100 Mbps and above  
  Outer Pererenan, Cemagi, Bukit   Fibre in places, patchy in others  
  Tabanan, North Bali, remote plots   Often no fibre; mobile or satellite  

The variation is street by street rather than area by area. A villa 400 metres from a fibre served road may not be served itself, and getting a line extended is a cost and a wait rather than a phone call.

  Check availability at the exact address before you commit  , particularly if you work from home. Do not accept "the area has fibre" as an answer.

   Providers

Biznet and MyRepublic are the common fibre providers in expat areas. IndiHome, the Telkom service, has the widest coverage and more variable performance.

Business packages cost more and generally come with better support and, in some cases, an SLA. For anyone whose income depends on the connection, that is worth paying for.

   Mobile as backup

Mobile data is cheap, fast and widely available, and it is the practical backup for everyone here. Telkomsel has the best coverage, particularly outside the south.

A local SIM with a generous data package, plus a phone that tethers, covers you when the villa line drops. This is not an edge case, it is a normal part of working here.

   Weather

Heavy rain degrades connections, and wet season runs roughly November to March. Outages during storms are common and usually short.

Power outages take the connection with them. A small UPS on the router costs very little and keeps you online through a short cut.

   Coworking

Canggu has the highest density of coworking spaces, Ubud has good options, Sanur has fewer but adequate ones. They exist partly because villa connections are variable, and a membership is a reasonable insurance poli

t: Is money moving from Dubai to Bali?
s: Dubai prices rose hard and yields compressed. Some of that capital went looking, and Bali caught part of it. Most of it is buying the wrong thing.
b:
The flow is real and the reasoning behind most of it is not.

   What happened in Dubai

A sustained run in prices after 2021, driven by residency reform, relocation of wealth, and a genuinely attractive tax position. Entry prices rose substantially and the easy yield compressed as they did.

That is the normal fate of a market that works. The money that arrived early did well, and later money faces a different arithmetic.

   Why some of it looks at Bali

  Entry price.   A Dubai deposit buys a whole villa here.

  Yield.   On a well bought, properly licensed property, net yields here can exceed what Dubai now offers, because the cost base is so much lower.

  Lifestyle.   Different product entirely, and for a certain buyer that is the actual driver.

   Why most of it buys badly

Buyers arriving from Dubai are used to a regulated market with a functioning registry, real comparables, financing and enforceable title.

None of that exists here. They apply Dubai habits: trust the agent, trust the projection, move quickly on a good looking deal.

The specific failures:

  Assuming "freehold" means what it means in Dubai. It does not exist for foreigners here
  Trusting a yield projection instead of twelve months of operating statements
  Using the seller's notary, because in a regulated market that is fine
  Not verifying zoning, because in Dubai the developer handled it
  Paying a deposit before verification

   The honest framing

Bali is not Dubai at a discount. It is a different market with weaker rights, no registry you can lean on, and a verification burden that falls entirely on the buyer.

The yield advantage is real and it is compensation for exactly that.

   What a buyer coming from Dubai should do differently

Appoint their own notary. Budget two to three weeks for verification. Model occupancy month by month. Treat the operating licence as a valuation input rather than paperwork. Value land and building separately.

Everything the Dubai system did for them

t: How do you actually make money from Bali property?
s: Most people only know nightly rental. It is the most competitive of the four and the one with the heaviest operating load.
b:
There is more than one way to be paid by a property here, and the obvious one is the hardest.

   The four routes

  One: nightly rental.   Highest gross revenue, highest costs, licensed activity, and the most competitive segment in the market. Staff, laundry, commission, management and a five year refurbishment cycle all come out of it.

  Two: annual leasing.   Lower headline rate, effectively full occupancy while leased, frequently paid a year in advance, almost no operating load. On a generic villa in an oversupplied corridor this often nets similarly with a fraction of the work.

  Three: land appreciation.   Buy well zoned land in a corridor before it develops and hold. No income, no operating costs, no licence required. This is where the largest gains here have actually been made, and it requires patience and capital you do not need.

  Four: build and sell.   Buy land, build, sell the completed asset. The margin is real and so is the execution risk: permits, supervision, cost overruns and a buyer pool at the end.

   Which one suits which buyer

  You are   Route  
             
  Present, hands on, differentiated property   Nightly rental  
  Absentee, want predictability   Annual leasing  
  Long horizon, capital not needed   Land  
  Experienced, willing to supervise   Build and sell  

   The mistake

Underwriting route one while living somewhere else. Nightly rental is a business with staff, guests, reviews and a licence. Run remotely through a manager you did not properly vet, it produces the gap between the projection and the bank statement.

   The licensing dimension

Routes one and four intersect with licensing hardest. Since 22 July 2026 the villa and homestay classifications are closed to new foreign owned company registration, which changes how a new project structures its operating side.

Routes two and three are considerably less exposed to that.

   Common questions

    How do foreigners make money from Bali property?
Nightly rental, annual

t: What happens if a Bali property deal goes wrong?
s: Litigation here is slow, expensive and uncertain for foreigners. Almost everything worth doing about a dispute happens before you sign.
b:
The honest position: your protection is the contract and the diligence, not the courts.

   Why litigation is a poor remedy

Indonesian civil proceedings are slow, frequently running years through first instance and appeals. They are conducted in Indonesian. Enforcement of a judgment against a counterparty with no traceable assets achieves nothing.

For a foreigner, add distance, language and the cost of local counsel across a multi year process.

None of that means the system does not work. It means litigation is an expensive last resort rather than a backstop you can rely on when structuring a deal.

   Where disputes actually come from

  Source   Prevention  
             
  Deposit paid before diligence   Written refund conditions tied to defined checks  
  Seller not the registered owner   Land office verification through your own notary  
  Boundary disagreement   Walk the boundaries against the certificate  
  Unregistered access rights   Confirm the right of way is registered  
  Extension clause dispute   Fix term, price, notice and successors in the lease  
  Developer non completion   Payments tied to inspected milestones  
  Nominee breakdown   Do not use one  

Every row is cheaper to prevent than to argue.

   Arbitration

Commercial contracts here frequently specify arbitration, often under BANI, the Indonesian national arbitration board. It is generally faster and more predictable than the courts, and awards are enforceable.

If you are signing a substantial construction or joint venture contract, the dispute resolution clause is worth negotiating rather than accepting as boilerplate. Specify the forum, the language, the seat and the governing law.

   Foreign judgments

A judgment from a foreign court is generally not directly enforceable in Indonesia. A contract governed by English or Australian law, litigated abroad, may produce a judgment you cannot enforce against Indonesian assets.

That is an argument for arbitration with an Indonesian seat,

t: Can you volunteer legally in Indonesia?
s: Unpaid work is still work under the enforcement test being applied. There is a category for volunteering, and people who skip it are the ones being detained.
b:
This is the category that catches the most well intentioned people, because the assumption that unpaid means unregulated is wrong.

   The rule that surprises people

  Payment is not the test. Activity is.  

Since the Dharma Dewata task force became operational in April 2026, unpaid volunteering, yoga instruction, wellness workshops and unpaid teaching have all been treated as work. Roughly 100 officers across the main expat areas detained 62 foreign nationals in the first three weeks.

You can be deported for an activity you were not paid a rupiah for.

   The proper route

Indonesia has a   volunteer visit visa   category. It requires a sponsoring organisation, usually the foundation, NGO or institution you will be working with.

That sponsor requirement is the point. It ties the activity to a recognised organisation that takes responsibility for it, which is what makes the volunteering lawful rather than informal.

   What counts as volunteering

Teaching at a school or community project. Working with an NGO or foundation. Environmental or conservation work. Construction or renovation on a charitable project. Animal welfare work.

If an organisation is directing your time and you are producing something for them, that is the category, regardless of money.

   The yoga and wellness problem

Teaching a class, running a workshop or holding a retreat is work. So is doing it for free, for exposure, or in exchange for accommodation.

Accommodation in exchange for teaching is   compensation  . So is a free villa stay in exchange for promotion. The absence of cash does not place an activity outside the definition.

   What to do

Ask the organisation which visa they sponsor volunteers on. A legitimate foundation will know and will have done it before.

If they tell you a tourist visa is fine, that is their risk assessment, not yours, and you are the one who gets deported and banned.

   Common questions

    Do I need a visa to volunteer in Indonesia?
Yes. There is a v

t: Is Kerobokan worth buying in?
s: Between Seminyak and Canggu, with real local infrastructure and prices that reflect the absence of a beach.
b:
Kerobokan is where a lot of Bali's actual functioning happens: hardware shops, warungs, clinics, furniture workshops and the roads that connect the tourist areas to each other.

   What it is

A working Balinese area with foreign residents layered over it, rather than a resort strip. Petitenget at its southern edge is effectively Seminyak. The northern end runs toward Canggu.

Prices drop noticeably the further you get from Petitenget and the main roads.

   Why it works for some buyers

  Price.   You are paying for location without paying for beachfront.

  Access.   Genuinely central. Seminyak, Canggu, the airport and Denpasar are all reachable without crossing the island.

  Services.   Everything practical is here, which matters more for a resident than for a guest.

  Rental.   Long stay demand is solid. Nightly demand exists but competes against properties that can offer a walkable beach.

   What to check

  Which end. Petitenget prices and northern Kerobokan prices are different markets
  Noise. Main roads here carry heavy traffic including trucks
  Zoning, which varies sharply across the area
  Drainage on the lower streets
  Whether the lane takes construction access

   The honest read

Kerobokan is not a destination and does not pretend to be. It is where you buy when you want proximity to three places at once and are not paying for a view.

For a resident, that is a strong proposition. For a nightly rental investor, it is a harder sell than the beach corridors and the numbers should reflect that.

   The sub areas that matter

  Petitenget   at the southern edge is effectively Seminyak: beach clubs, restaurants and Seminyak pricing.

  Umalas   to the north is quieter, more residential and family oriented.

  Central Kerobokan   along the main roads is commercial and dense, with the lowest prices and the most traffic.

  Western Kerobokan   toward Canggu picks up some of that corridor's demand without its prices.

   What it is genuinely good for

t: What does your money actually buy in Bali?
s: The same figure buys a different life here, and the gap is widest on exactly the things most people cannot buy at home any more.
b:
This comparison is usually made badly, by comparing a villa price to a house price. The useful version compares what a given monthly figure produces.

   USD 2,500 a month

  At home  , in most Australian, British, Dutch or North American cities: rent on a modest apartment, and not much else once bills are paid.

  In Bali  : a comfortable single life with room to spare. A decent villa or apartment, eating out regularly, a gym, a scooter, and help with cleaning.

   USD 5,000 a month

  At home  : a comfortable middle class life, probably with a mortgage taking a large share.

  In Bali  : a family with children in international school, which is the single largest line, plus a villa, staff and a car with a driver.

   What the money buys that it cannot at home

  Space.   A pool and a garden are ordinary here at prices that buy a flat elsewhere.

  Time.   Domestic help and drivers are affordable in a way they are not in most Western countries. That is hours back every week.

  Climate and outdoors, year round.   Not a small thing over a decade.

  Proximity.   Six hours from Perth, well connected across Asia.

   What it does not buy

  Ownership.   No freehold, ever, for a foreigner. Whatever you spend, you hold a lease, a right of use, or a company's building right.

  Medical depth.   Routine care is excellent value. Complex care is limited and evacuation runs USD 55,000 to 100,000.

  Certainty.   Your right to be here is renewable, and the rules have moved quickly.

  Infrastructure.   Traffic, water, waste and drainage are real constraints, not inconveniences.

   The honest arithmetic

Bali buys more life per dollar and less security per dollar. That is the trade, and it is a good one for people whose security is elsewhere and a poor one for people putting everything here.

   Common questions

    Is Bali really cheaper than living at home?
For daily life, substantially. For education, insurance and anything requiring imported goods or complex healthcare, t

t: How do you get an Indonesian driving licence?
s: An IDP endorsed for motorcycles covers a visit. If you live here, the local SIM removes the insurance argument entirely.
b:
Almost every foreigner here rides, and a large share of them are not licensed for what they are riding.

   The three positions

  Option   Covers you  
             
  IDP endorsed for motorcycles, with home licence   Yes, for visitors  
  Indonesian SIM C   Yes, and it is the right answer for residents  
  Car only IDP, riding a scooter     No    
  Nothing   No  

That third row is where most people sit without realising it. An International Driving Permit issued for cars does not cover you on a motorbike, and a large scooter may exceed what your home category permits anyway.

   Why it matters more than the fine

The roadside fine is not the point. Insurance is.

Many travel and health policies exclude motorbike accidents entirely, and most of the rest exclude them unless you hold the correct licence for the engine size. Scooter accidents are the leading cause of serious injury to foreigners in Bali.

A standard emergency case costs USD 5,000 to 25,000 without cover, and medical evacuation to Singapore runs USD 55,000 to 100,000. A denied claim turns an accident into a financial catastrophe.

Read that clause before you rent a scooter, not after.

   Getting an Indonesian SIM

  SIM C   covers motorcycles,   SIM A   covers cars. Application is made locally, requires your passport and stay permit, a health check and a theory and practical test.

For residents this is the sensible route. It is inexpensive, it removes the licensing argument entirely, and it lasts years rather than being tied to a trip.

Requirements differ for KITAS holders and visitors, and some categories are only open to permit holders. Check the current position locally before you go, and expect the process to take a morning.

   Practical safety

  A proper full face or open face helmet, not the rental shell
  Cover your skin; most Bali scooter injuries are road rash
  Avoid unlit roads at night, where edge markings and open drains are hazards
  Take rain seriously: surfaces go slick within se

t: When is the best time to visit Bali?
s: Dry season is easier and busier. Wet season is cheaper, quieter, and the only honest time to inspect a property you intend to buy.
b:
Bali has two seasons and they behave very differently, both for visitors and for anyone assessing property.

   The calendar

  Period   Character  
             
  April to June   Dry, warm, fewer crowds. Arguably the best window  
  July to August   Peak. Best weather, highest prices, heaviest traffic  
  September to October   Dry, quieter, still excellent  
  November to March   Wet season. Humid, afternoon downpours, cheapest  
  December to January   Wet, but busy again over the holidays  

Wet season does not mean constant rain. The typical pattern is a heavy downpour for an hour or two, often in the afternoon, then it clears. Mornings are frequently fine even in January.

   For a holiday

April to June and September to October are the sweet spot: dry weather without August prices or August traffic.

July and August deliver the most reliable weather and the worst of everything else. Canggu and Seminyak traffic in peak season genuinely changes how a day works.

   For a property trip, come in wet season

This is the part that matters commercially and almost nobody does it.

A road that floods in February looks perfect in July. Drainage, standing water, which lanes become impassable, whether a river rises, how a house handles humidity: none of it is visible in dry season.

Anyone buying land or a villa without seeing the area in wet season is inspecting half the property. Come in January or February, walk the plot in rain, and drive the route home at six in the evening.

   What it means for rental income

Occupancy drops in the wet months. Any yield projection that applies peak season occupancy across twelve months is describing a year that does not exist.

The shoulder months are where the annual number is actually decided, and they are the months sales material tends to skip.

   Nyepi

Bali's day of silence, usually in March, shuts the island completely for 24 hours. No flights, no traffic, no lights, nobody outside, including tourists in villas.

It is ex

t: Is buying property in Bali worth it?
s: For some buyers yes, for most of the ones being sold to, no. The difference is entirely in what you buy and what you verify.
b:
The honest answer depends on which version of the purchase you are actually making.

   When it is worth it

  You bought   land   that is well zoned, verified, and in a location with real demand
  The   structure is lawful   and in your name or your company's
  A   licence exists   and covers the building, if you intend to rent nightly
  The   price reflects   land value plus depreciated building, not a projection
  You have a   horizon long enough   to ride a soft year
  You   wanted to be here   anyway

   When it is not

  The price was set by a yield forecast rather than by the asset
  The rental licence is absent, assumed, or belongs to someone not in the deal
  It is one of two hundred near identical villas in the same corridor
  The lease has years already run and the extension clause says "market rate"
  You need the capital back within three to five years
  You bought it remotely, on trust, using the seller's professionals

   The comparison that matters

Against what alternative? Money here is illiquid, operationally demanding, exposed to regulatory change, held on a term limited right, and denominated in a currency you probably do not spend.

Against that risk profile, a return that merely matches a passive index at home is not compensation. It has to beat it clearly, and on a well bought property it can.

   What has actually changed

In roughly one year: 18 business classifications closed to new foreign owned registration, nominee facilitation criminalised, KBLI renumbered, and a dedicated immigration task force deployed.

Regulation moves faster here than the market cycle. Anyone underwriting on historical appreciation alone is watching the wrong variable.

   The version that works

Buy the land on verified fundamentals. Treat the rental business as a licensed business with real costs and real competition. Pay a price that works if the last three years do not repeat.

That is a narrower set of purchases than the market is selling, and it is the set t

t: Bali or Lombok for investment?
s: Lombok is a fraction of the price and a fraction of the demand. The question is whether you are buying income or buying time.
b:
The legal framework is identical because it is national law. Everything commercial is different.

   The comparison

    Bali   Lombok  
                   
  Land price   High and rising in the corridors   A fraction  
  Build cost   Low, deep contractor pool   Lower, fewer skilled contractors  
  Tourism volume   The regional benchmark   A small share of Bali's  
  International flights   Extensive   Limited  
  Rental demand   Mature, foreign operated villas   Thin, concentrated in the south  
  Resale pool   Deep in the main corridors   Shallow  
  Title irregularity   Present, manageable   More common  
  Professional services   Well established   Thinner  

   The Lombok case

South Lombok around Kuta, Selong Belanak and Mawun has genuine surf, genuine beauty and land at prices Bali passed fifteen years ago.

The Mandalika special economic zone was meant to be the catalyst, anchored by the MotoGP circuit and planned resort development. Some has been built. A good deal has not, on the original timeline or scale.

That is the pattern to price for. Buy on what exists, not on a masterplan.

   The Bali case

Demand that already exists, an airport with international connectivity, a mature villa rental economy, and an exit market with actual buyers in it.

You pay for all of that, and in the oversupplied corridors you can pay too much.

   The honest question

  Are you buying income or buying time?  

Bali produces income now, at a price that reflects it. Lombok is priced for growth that has not arrived, and may arrive slowly.

Both are legitimate. Confusing them is not. A Lombok purchase underwritten on Bali occupancy assumptions will disappoint, and a Bali purchase made because Lombok felt too slow usually means overpaying for the generic product.

   What to verify in Lombok specifically

Title history, which is more often irregular, particularly on land passed through inheritance without registration. Access rights, registered rather than customary. Zoning. And

t: Can you own a beach in Indonesia?
s: Nobody owns the beach. Understanding what those beachfront businesses actually hold explains a lot about what beachfront land is worth.
b:
Coastline in Indonesia is not private property. So the obvious question is what every beach club and beachfront villa is actually sitting on.

   The rule

The shoreline and the area seaward of it are state controlled. There is also a coastal border zone, a setback measured from the high water line, within which construction is restricted.

So a property marketed as beachfront is not selling you the beach. It is selling you land behind the setback, with access.

   What beachfront businesses hold

A land right on the parcel behind the boundary, plus permits for what they operate, plus in some cases specific authorisations for structures or activity closer to the water.

A beach club with loungers on the sand is generally operating under permission, not ownership. That permission is a licence position, and licence positions can change.

   Why this matters to a buyer

  The setback reduces your buildable envelope  , sometimes dramatically, on exactly the parcels that cost the most per are.

  Beachfront premiums are partly for access and view  , not ownership of the sand. That is a legitimate premium, but it is not what most buyers think they are paying for.

  Erosion and coastal change   affect where the boundary sits. A setback measured from a shoreline that moves is not a fixed line.

  Enforcement has tightened   on structures built inside setbacks, in Bali and nationally.

   What to verify on any coastal parcel

  The exact setback that applies at that location
  The buildable envelope after setback, KDB, KLB and green area
  Whether existing structures sit inside the setback, and whether they are permitted
  Access rights to the beach, registered rather than customary
  What the parcel looks like in wet season, and how the shoreline has moved

   The pattern worth noticing

The most expensive land on the island is frequently the most constrained. Buyers pay a premium per are and then discover the buildable footprint is a fraction of the parcel.

Establish the

t: Is Nusa Dua a good investment?
s: Gated, manicured, hotel-dominated and unlike anywhere else in Bali. The most controlled property environment on the island.
b:
Nusa Dua is a planned resort zone on the eastern side of the Bukit peninsula, developed deliberately rather than organically.

   What that means

Wide roads, maintained landscaping, security gates, a calm lagoon beach protected by reef, and large international hotel brands rather than independent villas.

It is the least Balinese feeling part of Bali and the most predictable.

   The investment position

  Factor   Nusa Dua  
             
  Entry price   High  
  Stock   Hotel dominated, limited private villas  
  Guest type   Conference, family resort, older travellers  
  Seasonality   Steadier than the west coast  
  Surf   Reef breaks that work in wet season  
  Airport   20 to 30 minutes  
  Independent villa demand   Thin. Guests here mostly want hotels  

The structural issue for a private buyer: Nusa Dua's demand is built around resort hotels. A private villa competes against full service properties with restaurants, spas and staff, which is a hard comparison to win.

   Where it makes sense

For owner occupiers who want security, quiet, maintained surroundings and reliable infrastructure, it is arguably the easiest place to live on the island.

For investors, the case is much weaker than the west coast unless the property is genuinely differentiated or sits in one of the branded residence schemes.

   Nusa Dua versus Jimbaran

Jimbaran is a working town with a fishing bay and a mix of villas and warungs, closer to the airport and considerably cheaper. Nusa Dua is controlled, manicured and more expensive.

For a private villa targeting independent guests, Jimbaran is usually the better economics. For resort adjacent stability, Nusa Dua.

   The branded residence model

Much of what a foreign buyer can actually purchase in Nusa Dua sits within hotel branded or resort managed schemes rather than as standalone villas.

That brings professional management, a maintained environment and an existing guest pipeline. It also brings management agreements with fee st

t: How do you extend a KITAS?
s: Extensions are not automatic and the deadlines are unforgiving. The bigger risk is that a lapse resets your path to permanent stay.
b:
Most KITAS problems are not refusals. They are people starting too late.

   The basics

A KITAS is issued for a defined period and extended while the underlying basis still holds: the job, the company, the marriage, the investment, the retirement status.

Extension is applied for   before expiry  , through your sponsor. Leave it to the final days and a single missing document becomes an overstay.

   Start early

Begin at least a month out, more if any supporting document needs renewing, legalising or translating.

Documents that commonly hold things up: a company's tax filings, an LKPM report that was never submitted, a marriage certificate needing legalisation, a passport with under six months validity.

   Your sponsor carries the process

Whoever sponsors the KITAS applies for the extension. That is your employer, your PT PMA, your spouse, or an agent.

  This is the dependency people underestimate.   If the sponsoring company has fallen behind on its own compliance, missed LKPM reporting, or had its NIB suspended, your extension is exposed. Company compliance is a personal matter when your residence depends on it.

   What a lapse actually costs

Beyond the fine and the immediate problem, a gap in your permit history can   reset your qualifying period for KITAP  .

If you are working toward permanent stay through consecutive years on an appropriate KITAS, a lapse can put you back to the start. People discover this years later when they apply and are told the clock restarted.

If KITAP is the destination, treat continuity as the thing you are protecting.

   Changing category

Moving between KITAS types, from work to investor, or investor to family, is not an extension. It is a new application, and it can also affect your KITAP count.

Take advice before switching rather than after.

   Common questions

    How early should I apply to extend a KITAS?
At least a month before expiry, and earlier if any supporting document needs renewing, legalising or translatin

t: How do you value a property in Bali?
s: Value the land and the building separately, then check both against what the property can lawfully earn. Asking prices are not evidence.
b:
Most buyers here value a property by comparing it to other asking prices. In a market where listings sit for months at no cost to the seller, that is comparing fiction to fiction.

   The method

  Step 1: value the land.   Establish price per are for comparable, similarly zoned land on the same road, from   transacted   evidence verified by your notary. Multiply by plot size.

  Step 2: value the building.   Estimate what it would cost to construct today at USD 600 to 1,500 per square metre by specification, then depreciate hard. Tropical wear is fast and a full refurbishment cycle runs roughly every five years.

  Step 3: value the fit out.   Furniture and soft goods are short lived here. A four year old fit out is much closer to replacement than to new.

  Step 4: sanity check against lawful income.   Only what the property can legally produce, given its licence position. An unlicensed villa's rental income is not a valuation input.

Add steps 1 to 3, check against 4. Where the asking price sits far above, ask what justifies the gap.

   Leasehold changes everything

A leasehold is a wasting asset. Its value should decline as the term runs down, steeply toward the end, and the extension clause determines how steeply.

Buyers regularly pay near freehold prices for leaseholds with a third of the term gone and an extension clause saying "market rate". That combination is the worst value proposition commonly available here.

   The deductions that are real and quantifiable

  Issue   Effect on value  
             
  Short remaining term   Severe, and non linear  
  Weak extension clause   Severe  
  Missing PBG or SLF   Large, and shrinks the buyer pool  
  Licence absent or non transferable   Treat rental income as zero  
  Fit out due for refurbishment   Cost of the refurbishment, or more  
  Narrow access road   Material, affects build cost and guests  
  Green zoning   Decisive, if you intended to build  

   Why asking prices run high

Listings cost the seller

t: How does leasehold work in Bali?
s: The instrument most foreign buyers here actually hold. It is a contract, not a title, and that distinction decides what happens when things go wrong.
b:
Most foreign held property in Bali sits on Hak Sewa, the right to rent or lease. Understanding exactly what that is prevents most of the disappointment in this market.

   What it is, precisely

A   contractual right   to use land for an agreed period, granted by the landowner. It is not a registered land title in the way Hak Milik, HGB and Hak Pakai are.

That single fact drives everything:

  Your right is against   a person  , not recorded in the land register as ownership
  It depends on the landowner's title being sound
  It depends on the contract binding successors
  It cannot usually be used as security for lending

   Why it is still the most common route

It requires no residency, no company, no minimum value and no capital threshold. A foreigner can sign a lease on the same day they arrive.

For a home you will use for a defined period, well drafted, it is a legitimate and widely used instrument.

   What makes one lease good and another worthless

  Clause   What to demand  
             
  Term   Stated in years, with the start date defined  
  Extension   A fixed term and a   fixed price or formula  , not "market rate"  
  Notice   A defined window with a consequence for late notice that is not forfeiture  
  Successors   Binds heirs, successors and any future owner of the land  
  Building   States what happens to the structure at expiry  
  Assignment   You may transfer it, and on what conditions  
  Registration   Noted so a purchaser of the freehold discovers it  

"Extendable at market rate" is the clause that ruins leases. It reads as a right and functions as the landowner's option, priced at the moment your alternative is walking away from a building you paid for.

   The wasting asset problem

A lease declines in value as it runs down, and the decline accelerates near the end. A right with eight years left trades far below half the value of the same property with thirty, because your buyer inherits the expiry.

Model that from day one rather th

t: Can you still buy in Bingin?
s: One of the most sought cliff positions on the Bukit, and the area where enforcement against unpermitted cliff structures has bitten hardest.
b:
Bingin is a narrow cliff cove on the Bukit's west coast, famous for the wave and for warungs built down the cliff face toward the sand.

   Why people want it

The setting is genuinely unrepeatable. A tight cove, a world class reef break, and a cliff edge with views that cannot be built inland.

Land with that outlook is finite in a way rice field land is not, which is the entire scarcity argument for the Bukit.

   The risk that defines this area

Bingin is the clearest example in Bali of what happens when structures are built inside coastal setbacks without proper permits.

Enforcement action against cliff and beachfront structures here has been real, and it has affected businesses that had operated for years. "It has been there a long time" is not a defence, and neither is "everyone did it."

If you are looking at anything on or near the cliff:

  Establish the exact coastal setback that applies at that point
  Confirm PBG and SLF exist and describe the structure as it stands
  Check whether any part sits inside the setback
  Assume enforcement continues rather than relaxes

A structure inside a setback cannot be regularised at any price. That is the difference between a paperwork problem and a demolition.

   The practical constraints

  Constraint   Reality  
             
  Access   Steep, narrow, often on foot for the last stretch  
  Water   Limestone Bukit. Supply is a real operating cost  
  Construction   Difficult and expensive on cliff terrain  
  Parking   Genuinely scarce  
  Distance   Long drives to schools, hospitals, the west coast  

   The honest position

Land set back from the cliff, correctly zoned and permitted, in an area with this much demand, is a good asset.

A cliff structure with vague paperwork is the single riskiest thing you can buy in Bali, and the price should reflect that rather than the view.

    Can foreigners buy property in Bingin?

t: How do you extend a visa on arrival?
s: Thirty days extendable once, done online or through an agent. Apply on day 29 and a single rejected document becomes an overstay.
b:
The extension itself is routine. Almost everything that goes wrong is timing.

   What you get

     
             
  Initial stay   30 days  
  Extensions permitted     One    
  Extension length   A further 30 days  
  Maximum total   60 days  

After that, you leave. There is no second extension, and staying beyond it is overstay with daily fines from the first day.

   How to do it

  Online  , through the official immigration system, or   through an agent   for a modest fee. Agents handle the paperwork and any biometric or office attendance requirement.

For a single extension, an agent is usually worth it. The fee is small against the cost of getting it wrong.

   Start at least a week early

The single most common failure is applying at day 28 or 29, having a document rejected, and running out of runway.

Give yourself a week. If something is wrong with your passport validity, your photo, your address details or your onward ticket, you want time to fix it rather than discovering it on the last day.

   What you need

Passport with sufficient remaining validity, the VOA receipt, proof of address in Indonesia, and depending on the route, an onward ticket.

Passport validity catches people. Requirements are typically six months from entry, and a passport that was fine on arrival can create a problem at extension.

   Counting the days

Count from the date   stamped on entry  , not the date you think you arrived and not your flight date. Treat the expiry as the last day you may be in the country, not the day you intend to leave.

   When you need something else

If you intend to stay beyond 60 days, work remotely, run a business, retire here or join family, the VOA is the wrong instrument. The E33G covers remote work for a foreign employer, and investor, family and retirement routes exist for the rest.

   Common questions

    How many times can you extend a Bali visa on arrival?
Once, for a further 30 days, giving 60 days in total.

    Can I extend a VOA onlin

t: How bad is Bali traffic?
s: Distances here are measured in minutes, not kilometres, and the two diverge badly. It should change where you buy.
b:
This is the daily reality that most affects quality of life here, and the one visitors underestimate because they experience it for two weeks rather than every day.

   The problem

Bali's road network was built for a fraction of the current traffic. Roads are narrow, there are few alternative routes, and the volume of scooters, cars, delivery vehicles and construction traffic has grown far faster than the infrastructure.

The result is that a 12 kilometre journey can take an hour. Not occasionally, predictably, at the times you actually need to travel.

   Worst areas

  Area   Position  
             
  Canggu and Berawa   The worst on the island, and getting worse  
  Seminyak and Kerobokan   Dense, constant  
  Denpasar approaches   Heavy at commuter hours  
  Ubud centre   Congested, especially midday  
  Sanur   Comparatively light  
  Bukit interior   Light, but everything is far  

   What it should change about buying

  Drive the routes you will actually drive, at the hours you will actually drive them.   The school run at eight, the trip home at six, the airport at the hour your flights land.

This single exercise reorders most people's shortlist, and almost nobody does it before committing.

  If you have children, choose the school first  , then live near it. An hour each way twice a day is four hours of a parent's day, permanently.

  If you are buying rental property  , traffic is now a commercial factor. A villa two kilometres from a beach club that takes twenty five minutes at six in the evening gets that reflected in guest reviews and repeat bookings.

   Getting around

  Scooter   is fastest and by a wide margin the most dangerous. It is the main physical risk foreigners face here.

  Car with driver   is inexpensive and the sensible option for families, airport runs and wet season.

  Ride hailing   (Grab and Gojek) is cheap and widely available, though some areas restrict pickups because of local transport arrangements.

  Walking   is viable i

t: How do you extend a retirement KITAS?
s: Extension depends on the qualifying conditions still being met, and the one that changes with age is insurance rather than income.
b:
The retirement permit extends while the basis on which it was granted continues to hold. That sounds obvious and it is where the problems sit.

   What has to still be true

The age requirement, the income or savings evidence, accommodation, and whatever else the current criteria specify. These have been revised more than once, so confirm the present requirements rather than the ones that applied when you first applied.

   The condition that quietly changes

  Insurance.   Premiums climb steeply with age, some policies impose entry or renewal age limits, and pre existing conditions accumulate.

A retiree who qualified comfortably at 60 can find the same cover materially more expensive at 70, or unavailable from the same provider.

This matters beyond the permit. Routine care in Bali is good and cheap, but complex care is thinner and   medical evacuation to Singapore runs USD 55,000 to 100,000  . Your policy needs evacuation cover of at least USD 100,000 to 250,000, named explicitly.

Check your renewal terms well before you need them, not when the permit is due.

   Start early

A month minimum, more if documents need renewing or legalising. Passport validity, proof of funds, and any insurance documentation all take time to assemble.

   Continuity and KITAP

Consecutive years on an appropriate KITAS build toward   KITAP  , permanent stay, which means fewer renewals and a more stable footing for Hak Pakai ownership.

A lapse can reset that count. If permanent stay is the destination, protect the continuity above almost everything else.

   The property connection

Hak Pakai, the only route by which a foreigner holds a registered land right in their own name, requires valid residency.

If you hold property that way and let the permit lapse, there are consequences to understand rather than discover. Leasehold and company held property are less exposed, which is one reason buyers uncertain about staying long term favour those structures.
