    How

t: What do all the Bali property terms mean?
s: Every Indonesian term a foreign buyer will meet, in plain English, with what it actually means for you.
b:
Indonesian property documents are in Indonesian, and the terms are not intuitive. These are the ones that decide things.

   Land titles

  Hak Milik (SHM)   Freehold. Perpetual. Indonesian citizens only. Never available to a foreigner.

  Hak Guna Bangunan (SHGB)   Right to build. Held by Indonesian legal entities including a PT PMA. Defined term, extendable.

  Hak Pakai (SHP)   Right of use. The only registered land right a foreigner can hold personally, requiring valid residency and meeting minimum value conditions.

  Hak Sewa   Lease. A contract, not a registered title. What most foreign buyers here actually hold.

  Hak Guna Usaha (HGU)   Right to cultivate, for agricultural enterprise.

  Girik / Petok   Not a certificate. Customary or tax evidence of possession on unregistered land. Trades at a discount for good reason.

   People and documents

  Notaris   Public notary who draws up deeds generally.

  PPAT   Pejabat Pembuat Akta Tanah. The official authorised specifically to make land deeds and lodge transfers. A transfer is not effective without one.

  BPN   The national land agency, where certificates are verified.

  AJB   Akta Jual Beli, the deed of sale and purchase executed before a PPAT.

   Building and zoning

  PBG   Persetujuan Bangunan Gedung. Building approval, required   before   construction. Replaced IMB.

  SLF   Sertifikat Laik Fungsi. Certifies the finished building is fit for use.

  KDB   Building coverage ratio. Maximum share of the plot the footprint may occupy.

  KLB   Floor area ratio. Total built floor area relative to plot size.

  KDH   Minimum green area that must stay unbuilt.

  Zona hijau   Green zone. Agricultural. Generally cannot host tourism accommodation.

   Company and licensing

  PT PMA   Foreign owned limited liability company.

  NIB   Nomor Induk Berusaha. Business identification number issued through OSS.

  OSS   Online Single Submission. The licensing system.

  KBLI   The classification code for a business

t: How risky are earthquakes and volcanoes in Bali?
s: Bali sits on an active margin. It rarely affects daily life and it should affect how you build, insure and choose a location.
b:
Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, and Bali is part of that. This is not a reason to avoid the island. It is a reason to make a few decisions deliberately rather than by default.

   The actual risk

  Earthquakes.   Felt tremors are not unusual. Damaging earthquakes are infrequent but real: the 2018 Lombok sequence caused serious damage and fatalities on the neighbouring island and was strongly felt in Bali.

  Volcanoes.   Mount Agung in the east is active, with significant eruptive episodes in 2017 and 2018 that triggered evacuations within the exclusion zone and repeatedly closed Ngurah Rai airport. Mount Batur is also active.

  Tsunami.   A low probability, high consequence risk affecting low lying coastal areas.

   What it means for buying

  Location.   Distance from Agung's exclusion zones matters in the east. Elevation matters on the coast. Neither should dominate the decision, but both belong in it.

  Construction standards.   This is the item within your control. Reinforced concrete frames built to proper standards perform well. Poorly detailed reinforcement, weak connections and unengineered additions do not.

Ask who the structural engineer was and whether the design was engineered rather than copied. On an existing building, a structural survey is worth the cost.

  Extensions.   Unpermitted additions are frequently the weakest part of a building, because they were built without engineering. That is a seismic problem as well as a licensing one.

   Insurance

Earthquake and volcanic cover is sometimes included, sometimes an extension, sometimes excluded. Confirm the treatment explicitly and in writing rather than assuming it sits inside a standard policy.

Insurers can also decline where PBG and SLF are missing, which turns a permit gap into an uninsured seismic exposure.

   Airport closure

The practical consequence most owners actually experience is ash closing the airport. It has happened repeatedly and it strands guests and cancels boo

t: How do you negotiate a property in Bali?
s: Feel does not move a seller. Verified defects do. Every item below is a number you can put on the table.
b:
Negotiation here is not haggling. It is presenting verified findings and letting them price themselves.

   What actually moves price

  Remaining term.   If the lease has years run, the value has already fallen. Bring the arithmetic.

  The extension clause.   "Market rate" is a defect. Price it as one.

  Missing PBG or SLF.   Quantify the regularisation cost, or treat the building as unpermitted and price land plus depreciated structure.

  No transferable licence.   Rental income becomes zero in your model. This is the largest single deduction available and sellers resist it hardest, because the income is what justifies their price.

  Refurbishment due.   Tropical fit out has a five year cycle. If it is due, that is a cost you are inheriting.

  Access road width.   Affects build cost, guest experience and resale.

  Time on market.   Public information if you ask. A property listed eleven months has already told you something.

   What does not move price

Telling a seller it is too expensive. Comparing to asking prices elsewhere. Enthusiasm. Deadlines you invented.

   The structural advantage you have

This is a   cash market  . Foreigners cannot realistically get local financing, so your buyer pool at exit is cash buyers, and so is theirs.

That means a verified, ready, funded buyer is genuinely scarce, and being obviously able to complete is leverage. Say it plainly and early.

   On manufactured urgency

Another buyer is looking. The price rises Monday. The owner needs to close this week.

Land listed for eight months does not become urgent because you walked onto it. If a seller will not allow time for standard verification, the verification is the reason.

Walking away is the only real leverage anyone has in any negotiation, and in this market it is available constantly because there is always another plot.

   Structure the payment, not just the price

Even at an agreed price, condition each tranche on a verification milestone that has actually been me

t: Is Nusa Lembongan worth buying?
s: Thirty minutes from Sanur by boat, genuinely beautiful, and constrained by water, power and a resale market of almost nobody.
b:
Nusa Lembongan sits between Bali and Nusa Penida, connected to Nusa Ceningan by a yellow bridge. Small enough to cross in twenty minutes.

   What is there

Surf breaks, mangroves, diving, seaweed farming that has largely given way to tourism, and a compact accommodation market of villas and small resorts.

Day trippers from Bali dominate arrivals. The overnight market is real but much smaller than the visitor numbers suggest.

   The constraints

  Constraint   Reality  
             
  Water   Limited. Desalination or shipped supply is normal  
  Power   Improved via undersea cable, still fragile  
  Waste   A visible problem on a small island  
  Construction   Every material arrives by boat, raising cost and time  
  Medical   Basic. Anything serious means a boat to Bali  
  Transport   No cars in most areas. Scooters and small trucks  
  Resale   Very thin  

That last row is the one buyers underweight. The pool of people who want to own on Lembongan and can lawfully do so is small, and it does not grow quickly.

   The demand pattern

Heavily seasonal and weather dependent. Rough seas cancel crossings, which cancels arrivals you had already counted on. A property underwritten on mainland occupancy assumptions will disappoint.

   Who it suits

Operators who will be present and run the business themselves, with a long horizon and no need for liquidity.

It does not suit passive investors, and it does not suit anyone who may need to sell within five years.

   What to verify

Water supply and its monthly cost in full occupancy. Power arrangements and backup. Title, through a mainland notary you appointed. Access rights. Boat logistics for construction. And realistically, who buys it from you.

   Where people actually buy

  Jungutbatu   on the northwest coast has the harbour, most of the accommodation and the best infrastructure.

  Mushroom Bay   is smaller and more resort oriented.

  The southern cliffs   have the dramatic outlooks and the hardest access, wa

t: Should you manage your Bali villa yourself?
s: A manager costs a large share of revenue. Self-managing costs your time and requires someone local you trust. Both are real options.
b:
Most owners assume a management company is compulsory. It is not, and the arithmetic is closer than the industry suggests.

   What a manager actually does

Guest communication, check in and check out, cleaning coordination, maintenance, supplies, listing management, pricing, and reporting.

The fee is a percentage of revenue, and the headline percentage is rarely the total. Booking commission, laundry, consumables, marketing, maintenance coordination and contractor markups are frequently billed separately.

   The real cost

Ask for a full sample month of actual statements from a comparable property under the same manager. Total everything charged, divide by the revenue, and compare that to the headline percentage.

Owners are routinely surprised by the gap.

   What self managing requires

  Need   Reality  
             
  A trusted local person   Non negotiable. Someone must physically be there  
  Guest response   Platforms rank on it. Hours, not days  
  Cleaning and laundry   Reliable, on turnover timing  
  Maintenance   A plumber, an electrician, a pool technician you can call  
  Listing and pricing   Ongoing work, not set and forget  
  Your presence   At least occasionally, and ideally in the first months  

Self managing from another time zone with nobody local is not self managing. It is neglect with a login.

   The middle option most people miss

Employ your own villa manager directly rather than contracting a management company. You carry the employment obligations, BPJS at roughly 14 percent and the THR month, and you keep control of the listing, the reviews and the calendar.

For a single villa with enough revenue to support it, this frequently nets better than a percentage of revenue agreement.

   The clause that decides everything

  Who owns the platform listing.   If the manager owns the account, reviews and calendar, changing manager means starting from zero, and that is leverage handed over for nothing.

Insist the accounts are in your name

t: Can you get permanent stay through employment?
s: Consecutive qualifying years on a work KITAS open the door to permanent stay. Continuity is the whole requirement and it is easy to break.
b:
KITAP is permanent stay, and the employment route reaches it through time rather than money.

   How it works

Consecutive years holding an appropriate work KITAS, sponsored by the same kind of employment relationship, build toward eligibility.

The exact qualifying period and conditions should be confirmed against current rules, because they have been adjusted. What has not changed is the principle:   continuous, properly documented residence on the right category  .

   What breaks the clock

  A gap between one KITAS expiring and the next being issued
  Switching category, for example work to family or investor
  Leaving Indonesia for an extended period
  A sponsoring employer falling out of compliance so the permit lapses

That last one is the underestimated risk. Your permit rests on the employer's standing. If the company misses filings or has its licence suspended, your continuity is exposed through no fault of your own.

   What KITAP gives you

    Work KITAS   KITAP  
                   
  Validity   Shorter, renewed regularly   Longer, fewer renewals  
  Admin load   Annual cycle   Periodic  
  Hak Pakai ownership   Supported   Supported, more stable footing  
  Banking and admin   Workable   Easier  
  Dependence on sponsor   High   Reduced  

For anyone intending to stay, the reduction in renewal exposure is the real prize. Every renewal is a point of failure, and KITAP removes most of them.

   Permanent is not unconditional

KITAP can be revoked: extended absence, breach of conditions, criminal matters. It also requires periodic reporting and re endorsement.

Permanent describes the term, not immunity from the rules.

   The property angle

Hak Pakai, the only registered land right a foreigner holds in their own name, requires valid residency. Holding it on an annually renewed permit means your registered right depends on a process you repeat every year.

On KITAP it does not. For anyone buying a home here to keep, that stability is the practical argu

t: How do you pay for a property in Bali?
s: Bank transfer, in your own name, to the registered owner, against written conditions. Every alternative exists to make somebody else's life easier.
b:
This is where money is actually lost in Bali, and the rules that prevent it are simple.

   The only acceptable method

Bank transfer, from an account   in your own name  , to the   registered owner   or the notary's designated account, documented, against a written contract stating what the payment is for.

Keep the transfer instruction, the confirmation, the contract clause it corresponds to, and a receipt identifying who received it and why.

   What to refuse

  Suggestion   Why  
             
  Cash for part of the price   Untraceable, usually paired with under declaring  
  Payment to an agent's account   The agent is not the seller  
  Payment to a third party company   You cannot verify who controls it  
  A different account for tax reasons   The tax reasons are not yours  
  Transfer before documents are ready   Urgency is the technique  

   Currency and cost

Large transfers are exposed to the rate on the day and your bank's spread. On a property sum that spread can exceed everything you paid your lawyer. Specialist transfer services generally price better than a high street bank.

If you are funding a build in stages over a year, the rate moves across the whole period. Some buyers fix part of it forward. Most never consider it.

   Do you need an Indonesian account?

For the purchase, no. Transferring from your home account directly is normal and works. Banks here generally require a KITAS or KITAP, so on a visitor visa you usually cannot open one anyway.

You need the account afterwards, for staff, utilities, contractors and tax.

   Staging the payments

Condition every tranche on a verification milestone that has actually been completed, with the refund position written down.

A seller who agrees the price but refuses conditional payment is telling you where the problem is.

   Under declaring

You will be offered it, framed as saving tax. It creates a documented purchase price lower than what you paid, which reduces your cost base on eventual sale

t: Is Seseh the next Pererenan?
s: Black sand, a golf course, temples on the beach and a wave of construction arriving from the south. Early, but no longer secret.
b:
Seseh sits immediately north of Cemagi, at the point where the developed west coast corridor starts to thin out.

   What is there now

A black sand beach with a temple on it, a golf course, rice fields, and villas arriving at pace from the Pererenan direction.

It is roughly where Pererenan was in 2019: the infrastructure is behind the construction, and the character is changing faster than the roads are.

   The investment case

  Price.   Below Pererenan and well below Canggu, for coastline in the same corridor.

  Trajectory.   Development has moved north along this coast for twenty years. Seminyak, then Canggu, then Pererenan. Seseh is the next section of that line.

  Beach.   Uncrowded, dramatic, with strong currents in places.

   The risk

The same one Pererenan carries, one stage earlier. A large volume of near identical villas is being built, and rental demand here is thinner than three kilometres south.

If you buy a generic three bedroom pool villa in Seseh underwritten on Canggu occupancy, the numbers will not hold. Guests still concentrate where the cafes are.

Buying   land   here is a more defensible thesis than buying a rental business.

   What to verify

  Zoning on the parcel. Much of the surrounding land is agricultural
  Access road width, for construction and for guests
  Drainage and standing water in wet season
  Distance to Pererenan and Canggu at 6pm, not at 10am
  How many comparable villas are under construction within a kilometre

   Who it suits

Buyers with a five to ten year horizon who want coastline at a price the developed corridor no longer offers, and who do not need income in year one.

   Common questions

    Where is Seseh in Bali?
On the west coast immediately north of Cemagi and Pererenan, roughly 15 to 25 minutes from Canggu depending on traffic.

    Is Seseh a good investment?
As a land play with a long horizon, it has a credible case. As a nightly rental business, demand is thinner than the corridor to the south.

t: Do you need to speak Indonesian in Bali?
s: You can live here on English alone. You will pay more, understand less, and stay outside most of what is actually happening.
b:
English is widely spoken in the tourist and expat areas, which is why so many foreigners live here for years without learning anything. It is also why they keep paying tourist prices.

   Why it is worth learning

  Bahasa Indonesia is genuinely easy   by the standards of world languages. No tenses in the European sense, no grammatical gender, no cases, no tones, and it uses the Latin alphabet. Pronunciation is consistent and phonetic.

You can reach useful conversational level in months rather than years, which is not true of Thai, Vietnamese or Mandarin.

  Prices change.   The foreigner price and the local price are different, and speaking the language moves you toward the second one. Over years of contractors, staff, markets and services, that is real money.

  Everything administrative is in Indonesian.   Contracts, permits, notary documents, tax filings. You will still use professionals, but understanding what you are signing is worth something.

  Staff relationships.   If you employ people, communicating directly rather than through a manager changes the relationship entirely.

   Balinese is different

Bahasa Indonesia is the national language and what you should learn.   Balinese   is a separate regional language with its own registers, spoken at home and in ceremony across the island.

Nobody expects a foreigner to learn Balinese. A few words are received warmly precisely because it is unexpected.

   How to learn

Private tutors here are inexpensive by Western standards and widely available. An hour or two a week with a tutor, plus using it daily, moves quickly.

Apps help with vocabulary and are poor at conversation. The bottleneck for most people is not knowing words, it is being willing to use them badly in public.

   What to learn first

Numbers, prices and bargaining. Directions. Food and ordering. Greetings and the polite forms. The vocabulary around your own house: repairs, water, electricity, deliveries.

That practical core covers most daily in

t: Where do you work from in Bali?
s: Canggu has the density, Ubud the quiet, Sanur the people who actually want to work. All three beat a villa connection you cannot rely on.
b:
Coworking exists here for two reasons: villa internet is variable, and working alone in a villa for six months is worse than people expect.

   The areas

  Canggu   has the highest density of spaces, cafes and other remote workers, and the strongest networking. It also has the island's worst traffic and the most people who are here to talk about working.

  Ubud   is quieter, cheaper, and oriented toward wellness, creative work and longer stays. Slower pace, fewer distractions.

  Sanur   has fewer spaces and a noticeably higher proportion of people who came to work rather than to network. It suits heads down focus.

  Uluwatu and the Bukit   have a small number of spaces serving the surf community, with everything a longer drive away.

   What it costs

Day passes, weekly and monthly memberships are all standard, and monthly is far better value than daily if you are staying. Private offices and dedicated desks cost more.

Against the price of a bad video call on a failing connection, a membership is cheap insurance for anyone whose income depends on being reachable.

   Cafes versus coworking

Cafe wifi in the main areas is generally good enough for email and browsing and unreliable for calls. Bandwidth is shared, noise is unpredictable, and there is a social limit to how long one coffee holds a table.

For calls, a coworking space with call booths is the difference between sounding professional and apologising.

   The time zone problem

Bali is UTC+8. That is comfortable with Asia and Australia, workable with Europe in your afternoon, and difficult with North America.

If your team is on the US East Coast, you are looking at consistently late nights. Work out the actual meeting times before you commit to living here, because a permanent 3am schedule erodes the reason you came.

   The visa point

Working remotely from Bali requires the right permit. The E33G covers people employed by or contracted to a company established outside Indonesia.

Working on a visitor

t: Can an investor get permanent stay in Indonesia?
s: The route exists, and it rests entirely on the PT PMA staying compliant for years. Your residence is only as good as your filings.
b:
The investor route to permanent stay is real, and it makes your company's housekeeping a personal matter.

   The path

Consecutive qualifying years holding an investor KITAS, with the underlying shareholding and the company both maintained in good standing, build toward KITAP.

Confirm the current qualifying period, since it has been adjusted.

   The dependency that decides it

Your investor KITAS rests on the PT PMA. The PT PMA carries continuous obligations:

  Obligation   Frequency  
             
  LKPM investment activity report   Quarterly for most classifications  
  Monthly tax filings, including nil returns   Monthly  
  Corporate income tax return   Annual  
  Financial statements   Annual  
  NIB and classifications current   Continuous  

Miss enough of these and the NIB can be suspended. A suspended NIB stops the company operating, and the permit resting on it is exposed.

  Years of compliance are what buy KITAP.   A single bad year of filings can cost the continuity you were building.

   The classification problem

Bali closed 18 low risk classifications to new foreign owned registration on 22 July 2026, including villa, homestay, real estate and management consultancy.

If your company was formed to operate one of those, confirm its position rather than assuming. An investor KITAS is granted in connection with a real business, and what the company can lawfully do determines whether that business exists.

   Do not let a dormant company drift

If the project stalls, the company keeps accruing obligations and penalties. Owners who stop paying attention discover years later that their compliance record, and their residence path, went with it.

Either stay minimally compliant or close it properly.

   What it costs

Accounting, monthly and annual filings, LKPM reporting, financial statements and corporate secretarial work are recurring costs. Budget them as a fixed annual line from year one.

A model that omits them is modelling a company that does n

t: Is Batu Bolong worth the premium?
s: The most walkable stretch in Canggu and the most expensive per are. Walkability is the whole product and it is genuinely scarce.
b:
Batu Bolong is the cafe strip running down to the beach in the middle of Canggu, and it is the closest thing Bali's west coast has to a high street.

   Why it commands a premium

  You can walk.   To coffee, to dinner, to the beach, to a gym. In an island where a two kilometre journey can take twenty five minutes at six in the evening, walkability is a genuine, scarce product.

Guests pay for it and reviews reflect it. A villa 400 metres off the strip and a villa eight hundred metres off it are different businesses.

   What you are paying for and against

  For   Against  
             
  Highest rental demand on the island   Highest entry price per are  
  Walkable to everything   Traffic and noise  
  Deepest resale market   Most competing supply  
  Consistent year round bookings   Little land, mostly older stock  

   The stock problem

Batu Bolong is built out. Most of what transacts is an existing building, often ten or more years old, and tropical wear is fast.

That means renovation is the realistic play here, and it means checking PBG and SLF on older structures and any extension carefully.

Much of the stock is leasehold with years already run. Establish the remaining term and the extension clause before you look at photographs.

   What to check

  Exact walking distance and route to the beach and the strip
  Noise, particularly on the lane at night
  Remaining term and the extension clause
  PBG and SLF matching the building as it stands, extensions included
  Parking, which is genuinely scarce and shows up in reviews
  Drainage on the lower lanes in wet season

   The honest verdict

If you are buying one property in Canggu and want it to fill a calendar without differentiation gymnastics, walkable Batu Bolong is the strongest position on the west coast.

You will pay for that, and the arithmetic still has to work at the price.

   Common questions

    Is Batu Bolong expensive?
It is among the highest per are on the west coast, driven by walkability

t: How long does due diligence take in Bali?
s: A clean title takes one to three weeks to verify properly. Anyone pressuring you inside that window is telling you something.
b:
Knowing how long this actually takes removes the seller's main weapon, which is urgency.

   The realistic schedule

  Days 1 to 3.   Appoint your own notary and legal reviewer. Obtain copies of the certificate, the seller's identity documents, and evidence of authority to sell.

  Days 3 to 7.   Certificate verified at the land office. Registered holder confirmed. Registered charges checked. Title type and remaining term confirmed against the record rather than the photocopy.

  Days 5 to 10.   Zoning checked on the specific parcel through the spatial planning system. Buildable envelope established from KDB, KLB, green area and setbacks.

  Days 7 to 12.   Boundaries walked against the certificate. Access route inspected and the right of way confirmed as registered rather than customary. Road width checked for construction access.

  Days 10 to 14.   For built property: PBG and SLF obtained and compared against the building as it stands, extensions included. Operating licence checked on OSS, including whether codes migrated to KBLI 2025 and whether it transfers.

  Days 12 to 21.   Spouse and heir consents. Tax receipts. Findings written up. Only now does a deposit make sense.

   What extends it

Inheritance in the title history. Unregistered or girik land. Disputed boundaries. Zoning questions. Multiple owners. A seller acting under power of attorney.

Each of these is a reason to slow down, not speed up.

   What should never compress it

Another buyer looking. A price rising Monday. An owner who needs to close this week.

Land listed for eight months does not become urgent because you walked onto it. If a seller will not allow two to three weeks for standard verification, the verification is the reason.

   The written output

Insist your notary puts the findings in writing: certificate authenticity, registered holder, title type, remaining term, encumbrances, zoning, boundaries, permits.

If it is not written down, it was not checked.

   Common questions

t: What do villas rent for in Bali?
s: Rates vary more by walkability and outlook than by postcode, and the annual number is set in the months nobody quotes.
b:
Published rates are peak season asking rates. The number that matters is what a property achieves across twelve months.

   What drives rate, in order

  Outlook.   An unrepeatable view, cliff or ocean, is the single largest premium available. Uluwatu and the Bukit cliffs sit at the top of the island's range for this reason alone.

  Walkability.   Batu Bolong and Seminyak command premiums because guests can walk to dinner. In an island where two kilometres takes twenty five minutes at six in the evening, that is a real product.

  Differentiation.   In corridors with hundreds of near identical three bedroom pool villas, the generic ones compete on price and the distinctive ones do not.

  Bedroom count and layout.   Groups pay more per head for larger villas, and the four bedroom market is less crowded than the three.

   The broad picture by area

  Area   Rate position   Occupancy pattern  
                   
  Uluwatu, cliff   Highest   Seasonal, shorter stays  
  Seminyak, Batu Bolong   High   Strong year round  
  Berawa, Echo Beach   High   Strong, swell and season weighted  
  Pererenan, Cemagi   Moderate to high   Heavy competing supply  
  Sanur   Moderate   Steadiest, longer stays  
  Ubud, Gianyar   Moderate   Less seasonal, lower ceiling  
  Tabanan, west   Low   Thin  
  North, east   Low   Very thin, short stays  

   The month that decides the year

July and August fill themselves. December fills. The annual figure is decided by February, March and November, and those are the months sales material does not discuss.

Model month by month rather than applying an annual average, and reduce year one substantially because a new listing has no reviews and no ranking.

   Long term rates

Annual leasing is a different market, frequently paid a year in advance. Canggu long term rentals start from around IDR 17.5M a month and rise sharply for anything with a private pool near the beach.

For generic villas in oversupplied corridors, annual leasing often nets

t: Is Canggu oversupplied with villas?
s: In the standard three-bedroom pool villa segment, yes. That is a yield problem before it is a land value problem, and the distinction matters.
b:
The question gets answered badly in both directions. Here is what the supply situation actually is.

   What happened

Between roughly 2021 and 2026 an enormous volume of villa construction landed in the Canggu and Pererenan corridor. Pererenan was rice fields in 2019.

Guest nights grew. Available villa nights grew faster.

   Where the oversupply actually is

  The standard three bedroom pool villa.   Open plan living, black and wood finish, rice field or garden outlook, priced in the same band. When two hundred functionally identical properties list in one corridor, they compete on price because nothing separates them.

That is the segment under pressure, and it is most of what is being built and sold.

   Where it is not

Differentiated property. An unrepeatable outlook, a plot size the market is not building, a walkable position, a four or five bedroom layout in a market saturated with threes.

Those fill. The pressure is on sameness, not on Canggu.

   Yield first, value later

Oversupply shows up as softer nightly rates and higher vacancy. That compresses yield immediately.

It moves property values only for properties whose price was set by yield in the first place, which is exactly the generic segment. Well zoned land in the corridor has held, because land scarcity and building oversupply are different facts.

   What it means for a buyer

  Do not pay a premium for the generic product at prices set when it was scarce
  Underwrite occupancy month by month and reduce year one hard
  Calculate break even occupancy and check how much room for error it leaves
  Favour properties that are not one of hundreds
  Remember Canggu still has the deepest rental demand and the only reliable resale market on the island

That last point is why "Canggu is finished" is wrong. Liquidity is worth real money, and it exists here in a way it does not in Tabanan.

   Common questions

    Is Canggu a bad investment now?
No, but the generic three bedroom pool villa in Canggu at 20

t: What should you know about Balinese culture?
s: Ceremony is not a tourist attraction here, it is the calendar. Understanding that changes how you build, hire and live.
b:
Bali is Hindu in a country that is overwhelmingly Muslim, and religious practice is woven into daily life to a degree foreigners consistently underestimate.

   Ceremony is the calendar

Temple ceremonies, family ceremonies, cremations and village obligations are frequent and take priority. Staff will need time off for them, and it is not negotiable in the way a foreign employer might assume a day off is.

Budget for it, plan around it, and treat it as a fixed feature of operating here rather than an inconvenience. Employers who fight it lose good staff.

  Nyepi  , the day of silence in March, shuts the entire island for 24 hours including the airport. No traffic, no lights, nobody outside, guests included. Plan bookings around it.

   Banjar

The banjar is the village community organisation, and it has real authority over what happens locally: construction, ceremonies, disputes, security, waste.

If you build or operate here, your relationship with the banjar matters more than most foreign owners expect. It can affect construction access, noise complaints, staff and whether small problems get resolved quietly or escalate.

Introduce yourself. Contribute when asked. This is not corruption, it is community obligation, and it is how the system works.

   Practical etiquette

  Step over offerings on the pavement, not on them
  Cover shoulders and knees at temples; a sarong is usually provided or required
  Do not enter a temple during menstruation, which is a stated rule rather than a suggestion
  Use the right hand for giving and receiving
  Do not touch heads, including children's
  Feet are impolite; do not point them at people or shrines
  Public anger loses you standing; raised voices are read as loss of control, not authority

That last one matters commercially. Negotiating hard is fine. Shouting marks you as someone to be managed rather than dealt with.

   The environment

Bali's waste and water problems are real and visible, particularly in wet season when r

t: What permit does a child of an Indonesian citizen need?
s: Indonesia allows limited dual citizenship for children of mixed marriages, with a choice that must be made by a deadline most families miss.
b:
This is the most consequential immigration question a mixed nationality family here faces, and it has a hard deadline attached.

   Limited dual citizenship

Indonesia does not generally permit dual nationality for adults. It makes an exception for   children of mixed marriages  , who may hold both nationalities until a set age.

At that point the child must   choose one  . The choice is not automatic and it is not indefinitely postponable.

   Why families miss it

The deadline arrives years after the paperwork was done, when the family has stopped thinking about it. Parents assume the status simply continues, or that a decision can be made later.

Missing the window can mean losing the Indonesian nationality by default, with consequences for land ownership, residence and the child's future options here.

  If you have a child of a mixed marriage, find out the exact deadline that applies to them and diarise it.   This is not something to discover late.

   Registration comes first

The dual status generally depends on the child being properly registered, which means birth registration, reporting where the birth occurred abroad, and the supporting documents legalised and translated.

A child who was never registered may not have the status the parents assume they have.

   If the child is not an Indonesian citizen

A foreign child of an Indonesian parent can hold a dependent permit sponsored by that parent. It grants residence, not the right to work, and it follows the sponsor's status.

   The property consequence

An Indonesian citizen child can hold   Hak Milik  , freehold. A foreign child cannot, and inheriting a title they cannot lawfully hold triggers a disposal requirement within a set period.

So the citizenship choice is also a property decision, and it interacts with whatever structure the family holds land through. Where a marriage has no prenuptial or postnuptial agreement separating assets, that compounds.

Take advice on immigration and property togeth

t: How do you convert a land title in Indonesia?
s: Moving land from a citizen's freehold to a right a foreigner or a company can hold is a normal procedure, and the gap between agreeing it and completing it is where money gets stuck.
b:
Most land a foreigner looks at is currently SHM, Indonesian freehold. You cannot hold that. So the transaction usually involves a conversion.

   The two common conversions

  SHM to SHGB.   Freehold converted to a right to build, held by an Indonesian legal entity such as your PT PMA. Standard when a company is acquiring land to develop or operate.

  SHM to Hak Pakai (SHP).   Freehold converted to a right of use held by a qualifying foreigner personally. Requires valid residency and meeting the minimum value conditions.

Both are established procedures handled by a PPAT and registered at the land office.

   Where it goes wrong

  Paying in full against a promise.   Buyers transfer the purchase price on the understanding that conversion will follow, then hold a receipt while the process stalls.

The certificate in the correct name is the product. Until it is issued, you hold a contract, not a title.

  Assuming eligibility.   Hak Pakai requires residency and a qualifying property value. If you do not meet both, the conversion you agreed cannot complete.

  Underlying title problems.   Conversion does not fix a defective title. Inheritance not resolved, boundaries disputed, charges registered, a spouse who never consented. These surface during conversion and stop it.

  Girik land.   Unregistered land must first be registered before anything else, which is a longer process that can surface competing family claims.

   How to structure the payment

Tie tranches to the conversion milestones: verification complete, deed executed, application lodged, certificate issued in your name. Final payment on the last one.

A seller who will not accept that structure is asking you to carry the entire risk of their own title.

   Timing and cost

Weeks to months depending on the land office and the complexity. Budget it into your schedule rather than assuming completion on deed signing.

Costs sit alongside the roughly 7 to 8 percent total transaction burden: buyer duty around 5

t: Is Kedungu the next investment corridor?
s: Where the west coast development wave meets Tabanan's cheap land. Real surf, real construction, and demand that has not caught up.
b:
Kedungu and Nyanyi sit on the Tabanan coast just north of Seseh, and they are where the corridor's northward march currently stops.

   What is happening there

Nyanyi hosts the Nuanu development, a large master planned project that has brought infrastructure, attention and a concentration of new accommodation to a stretch that had almost none.

Kedungu, slightly further north, has a surf beach, a river mouth, rice fields and a growing number of villas.

This is the most visible example in Bali of a corridor being created rather than grown.

   The investment case

  Price.   Tabanan pricing, which is a fraction of Canggu, for coastline in the same growth path.

  Catalyst.   A large master planned development nearby does change an area, and this one has.

  Surf.   Kedungu is a genuine break, which anchors a certain kind of demand independent of cafes.

   The risk

Demand here is currently produced by the development, not by the area. That is a meaningful distinction.

If the masterplan delivers at scale, the surrounding land benefits. If it slows, you own a villa in Tabanan with Tabanan rental demand and a Canggu adjacent purchase price.

Buy land on Tabanan fundamentals and treat the development as upside, rather than paying for the upside up front.

   What to verify

  Zoning on the parcel. Most surrounding land is agricultural
  Access road width and condition
  Water supply and monthly cost in full operation
  Drive time to Canggu and the airport at real hours
  How much accommodation is under construction within two kilometres

   Who it suits

Long horizon buyers who want coastline at Tabanan prices and can wait for demand to arrive. Not buyers needing income in year one.

   Common questions

    Where is Kedungu?
On the Tabanan coast north of Seseh and Cemagi, roughly 25 to 40 minutes from Canggu depending on traffic.

    Is Nyanyi a good place to invest?
It has a genuine catalyst in the nearby master planned development. Price the land on Tabanan funda

t: Is it better to buy from a developer or a private owner?
s: A developer gives you a new building and a company that may hold nothing. A private owner gives you a real asset and a title history you have to unpick.
b:
The risks are different in kind, not just in degree.

   Buying from a developer

  What you get.   A new or near new building, modern specification, sometimes a management arrangement and a yield projection.

  What you carry.   Construction risk if it is off plan. Counterparty risk, because many projects sit in a company formed for that project with no other assets. Specification risk, because what is delivered is what the contract says, not what the render showed.

  What to verify.   The land title held by the contracting entity now. PBG issued for the design sold. A completed project you can visit. Payments tied to inspected milestones.

   Buying from a private owner

  What you get.   An existing building you can survey, real operating history if it rents, permits you can check against what is standing, and a price that is usually more negotiable.

  What you carry.   Title history risk: inheritance, spousal consent, boundaries, charges. Building condition risk. And whatever the previous owner did without permits.

  What to verify.   Certificate at the land office. Registered holder and consents. Zoning. Boundaries walked. PBG and SLF matching the building including extensions. Whether the operating licence transfers.

   The asymmetry that matters

With a private owner, the problems are   discoverable now  . Everything wrong with the title and the building exists today and a proper two to three week diligence finds it.

With an off plan developer, the main risk is in the future and no amount of diligence eliminates it. You are betting on performance.

That is why the premium for completed property is usually money well spent.

   Where a developer is the better choice

An established developer with handed over projects you can walk through, verified land and permits, a realistic timeline, and payments following inspected progress.

That combination is genuinely safer than an unpermitted private villa with a tangled title.

   The question that separates the

t: How bad are Bali's water and waste problems?
s: Groundwater depletion and waste management are the island's real constraints, and both are becoming regulatory risks for property owners.
b:
This is the part of Bali that the marketing does not cover, and it increasingly affects owners commercially rather than only ethically.

   Water

Bali's water demand has grown far faster than its supply. Tourism is water intensive: pools, laundry, showers, golf, landscaping. Groundwater extraction has increased accordingly, and in parts of the south the water table has fallen.

For a property owner this shows up three ways:

  Operating cost.   Where piped supply is absent or insufficient, trucked water is a real recurring expense that rises in dry season.

  Regulatory risk.   Groundwater extraction is regulated and scrutiny has been increasing. A villa whose entire supply depends on an unpermitted well is carrying a risk that has been getting larger, not smaller.

  Long term viability.   A development model built on unlimited cheap groundwater is not a safe assumption for a twenty five year lease.

The Bukit is the sharpest example: limestone geology, little accessible groundwater, and many properties reliant on trucked supply.

   Waste

Bali's waste infrastructure has not kept pace with either population or tourism. Collection is inconsistent outside the main areas, landfill capacity is strained, and a significant share of waste is burned or ends up in rivers.

In wet season the rivers carry it to the beaches, which is why images of rubbish on Kuta beach circulate every year. It is seasonal, it is real, and it affects the product you are selling to guests.

   What owners can actually do

  Arrange proper waste collection rather than assuming it happens
  Separate and use the private recycling operations that exist
  Avoid burning, which is common and genuinely harmful
  Install water efficient fittings and a pool cover, which cuts evaporation substantially
  Harvest rainwater, which is straightforward here given the wet season volume
  Ensure any well is properly permitted
  Treat wastewater properly rather than to the minimum

   Why this is commercial

Gues

t: Is Pecatu or Ungasan better value than Uluwatu?
s: The interior Bukit, minutes from the famous breaks, at a fraction of clifftop prices. The trade is the view and the water.
b:
Pecatu and Ungasan are the inland villages on the Bukit peninsula, behind the cliffs that get all the attention.

   The price difference

Clifftop and ocean view land on the Bukit commands the highest premiums in Bali. Move a few hundred metres inland and the number falls dramatically for land that is minutes from the same breaks.

That gap is the entire opportunity here, and it is real. It is also entirely explained: you are buying access, not outlook.

   What you get

    Cliff   Pecatu / Ungasan interior  
                   
  Price per are   Highest on the island   Fraction of it  
  View   Ocean, unrepeatable   Limestone scrub, occasional distant sea  
  Nightly rate   Island top tier   Ordinary  
  Guest demand   View driven, strong   Depends on the property, not the plot  
  Water   Hard   Hard  
  Access   Often difficult   Better  

   The water problem is the same

The Bukit is limestone: porous, elevated and thin on accessible groundwater. Inland or on the cliff, the supply question is identical, and many properties rely on trucked water.

Ask how the property is supplied, what it costs monthly with the villa full in dry season, and what happens in a dry year. It is the question sellers here answer least convincingly.

   The realistic strategy

Interior Bukit rewards buyers who will build something people want to stay in regardless of the plot's outlook: a distinctive design, a good pool, genuine space, close to a named break.

It punishes buyers who assume Bukit proximity alone produces Bukit rates. It does not. The view produces the rates.

   What to verify

  Water supply and its real monthly cost
  Access road width for construction
  Zoning on the parcel
  Actual drive time to Uluwatu, Bingin and Padang Padang
  Distance to a supermarket and a clinic, which is longer than people expect

   Common questions

    Is Pecatu cheaper than Uluwatu?
Considerably, for interior land without the ocean outlook. Cliff and view plots are a different market e

t: What is SKTT and do you need a domicile letter?
s: Getting the KITAS is not the end of the process. Local registration is a separate step and people only discover it when something else is blocked.
b:
Foreigners assume the permit is the finish line. Local registration sits behind it and quietly gates other things.

   SKTT

  Surat Keterangan Tempat Tinggal   is the temporary residence registration, issued by the local civil registry once you hold a KITAS.

It records you as living at a specific address in a specific area. Think of it as the local half of your immigration status: immigration grants the permit, the local authority records where you actually live.

   Domicile letter

A   surat keterangan domisili   is a letter from the local administration confirming an address, for a person or a company.

For a company it is frequently required for licensing and banking. For an individual it comes up in administrative processes where an address must be evidenced.

   Why they matter more than they sound

These documents gate things:

    Bank account opening   often asks for address evidence
    Driving licence   applications may require local registration
    Company licensing   can require a domicile letter for the business address
    Some permit renewals   expect the registration to be current
    Administrative processes   generally run smoother with them in hand

People discover the gap at the point something else is refused, which is the expensive moment.

   When you move

Both are tied to an address. Move house and they need updating, and an address mutation may be required against your permit as well.

Foreigners routinely move within Bali and never update anything, then find the paperwork does not match at renewal.

   The virtual office question

Companies using a virtual office should confirm the provider can supply a valid domicile letter for the intended activity and regency. Some can, some cannot, and some banks refuse virtual addresses regardless.

Ask before committing to an address provider, not after the bank declines you.

   Common questions

    What is SKTT in Indonesia?
Surat Keterangan Tempat Tinggal, the temporary residence registration

t: What is moving to Bali actually like?
s: The first three months are the holiday. Months four to twelve are the ones that decide whether you stay.
b:
Almost everyone arrives with the same expectations and hits the same sequence.

   The arc most people follow

  Months 1 to 3.   Everything works. It is cheap, warm, and the life you imagined. This is the holiday continuing and it tells you nothing.

  Months 4 to 6.   Administration arrives. Visa renewal, a bank account you cannot open, a landlord dispute, a scooter accident or a near one, and your first wet season. The novelty stops carrying you.

  Months 7 to 12.   You either build a real life here or you start counting. Friends from month two have left. The social circle has to be rebuilt, and it will need rebuilding again.

   What people underestimate

  Wet season.   November to March. Not constant rain, but persistent humidity, flooded roads, mould, and an island that empties out. Anyone deciding to move should visit in February before committing.

  Administrative friction.   Nothing is one step. Permits, banking, utilities, imports. This does not improve with familiarity; you simply stop being surprised.

  Healthcare depth.   Routine care is good and cheap. Serious care is thin, and medical evacuation to Singapore runs USD 55,000 to 100,000.

  The transience.   The areas with the liveliest social scenes have the highest turnover. You will rebuild your friendships repeatedly.

  Visa reality.   Rolling tourist visas as a way of living here stopped being viable in April 2026. Living here properly means holding the permit matching what you actually do.

   What people overestimate

How cheap it is once you live properly. A comfortable single life runs USD 1,800 to 2,500 a month, a couple USD 2,500 to 3,500, and a family with international school USD 4,000 to 6,500.

How fast they will feel settled. A year is the realistic answer.

   What actually predicts staying

Foreign income that does not depend on being here. The correct permit. Insurance with evacuation cover. A reason to be here beyond escaping somewhere else.

t: Where should you buy around Ubud?
s: Central Ubud is congested and built out. The value and the views are in the villages around it, and each one behaves differently.
b:
Ubud itself is expensive, crowded and largely developed. The interesting decisions are in the ring of villages around it.

   The options

  Penestanan   sits on the ridge west of Ubud, reached by steps or a narrow road. Long established foreign community, walkable to Ubud, rice terraces on the plateau. The most convenient of the alternatives and priced accordingly.

  Sayan   overlooks the Ayung river valley to the west. The most dramatic outlook near Ubud and home to the best known luxury properties. Valley edge plots carry large premiums and severe building constraints.

  Tegallalang   runs north through the famous terraces. Cheaper, more agricultural, more of a drive, and increasingly built along the main road.

  Southern Gianyar  , toward Sanur, is cheapest and least Ubud like.

   The constraint that defines the area

Ubud's most beautiful plots are frequently the least buildable.

River valleys create the views and also create enforced setbacks. Green zone agricultural designation is widespread across Gianyar. A gorge edge plot with a spectacular outlook often means a building envelope pushed well back from the edge.

  Establish the buildable footprint before you value the view.   After setbacks, KDB, KLB and green area requirements, the number is often a fraction of the plot.

   Access is the second constraint

Many plots here are reached by lanes too narrow for construction vehicles. That raises build cost, lengthens timelines and limits guest access afterwards.

Walk the access route before you commit, and ask whether a concrete truck can reach the site.

   The demand pattern

Wellness, retreats, workshops and longer stays. Less seasonal than the coast, with a lower nightly ceiling. Occupancy can be competitive on an annual basis even where rates are not.

   Common questions

    Is Penestanan a good area in Ubud?
It is the most convenient of the surrounding villages, walkable to Ubud with an established foreign community and rice terrace outlooks.

t: When do you need a sworn translation?
s: Foreign documents generally need legalisation and a sworn translation before Indonesian offices will accept them, and the chain takes weeks.
b:
Almost every process that involves a document issued outside Indonesia runs into this, usually later than it should.

   What a sworn translation is

A translation by a translator officially recognised for the purpose, whose work Indonesian authorities accept. It is not the same as a competent translation by a bilingual friend or an agency without that status.

   The chain, in order

For a document issued abroad, the usual sequence is:

1.   Notarisation   in the issuing country
2.   Apostille or legalisation   in that country
3.   Sworn translation   into Indonesian

Each step depends on the one before it. Start the chain weeks before it is needed, because the foreign steps run on another country's timetable and you cannot accelerate them.

   What commonly needs it

  Marriage certificates, for spouse permits and asset separation agreements
  Birth certificates, for dependent permits and child registration
  Powers of attorney, for buying property remotely
  Corporate documents, for foreign shareholders in a PT PMA
  Police certificates and qualifications, for certain permits
  Wills and estate documents

   Where it bites in property

A   power of attorney   executed abroad so someone can sign for you at the deed needs the full chain. Arriving at the notary with an unlegalised document means the deed does not happen that day.

A   prenuptial or postnuptial agreement   for a mixed marriage, central to whether an Indonesian spouse can hold freehold cleanly, needs to be properly executed and recognised.

For   inheritance  , foreign wills and estate documents need the chain too, and the disposal deadline for a foreign heir holding a title they cannot lawfully hold does not pause while you arrange translations.

   Practical advice

Ask the Indonesian notary or office   exactly   which documents they need and in what form, before you start. Requirements differ between offices and between regencies, and doing the chain twice is expensive.

t: Is Bali running out of flight capacity?
s: Ngurah Rai is the constraint on arrivals, which makes it the constraint on rental demand. More villas do not create more visitors.
b:
Every rental projection assumes guests. Guests arrive on aircraft, and aircraft need slots.

   The constraint

Ngurah Rai is Bali's only international airport, and it has been operating close to its practical limit at peak times. Expansion has been discussed and worked on for years.

A North Bali airport has been proposed repeatedly across two decades without being delivered. Do not price land on it.

   Why this matters more than arrivals data

If seats are the binding constraint, then total visitor nights are capped by capacity rather than by demand.

Meanwhile villa supply in the main corridors has grown enormously. More rooms competing for a similar pool of guests is exactly the dynamic owners are experiencing as softer rates.

That is the mechanism behind the oversupply. It is not that people stopped coming. It is that the number who can arrive is limited while the number of beds is not.

   The second order effect nobody models

  Average length of stay has been falling   as Bali shifts toward shorter, higher frequency trips, particularly from Australia and regional Asia.

Shorter stays mean more turnovers for the same occupancy: more cleaning, more laundry, more consumables, more wear, more guest communication, for the same revenue.

That is a cost increase hidden inside a demand statistic, and it does not appear in any arrivals chart.

   What actually changes the ceiling

Airport expansion, new international routes, and larger aircraft on existing routes. All of which are outside your control and slower than construction.

   How to use this

Stop underwriting on island wide arrival growth. It tells you the size of the pool, not your share of it.

The questions that determine your occupancy are local: how many comparable properties within a kilometre, how many added in the last two years, how many under construction now.

   Common questions

    Is Bali airport at capacity?
It has been operating close to its practical limit at peak times, which constrains

t: Is East Bali coast worth buying?
s: Black sand, world-class diving and prices a fraction of the south. Rental demand is thin and seasonal, and that is the whole trade.
b:
Amed and Candidasa sit on Bali's east coast in Karangasem, facing Lombok across the strait.

   What is there

  Amed   is a string of fishing villages along a black sand coastline, built around diving and snorkelling. The USAT Liberty wreck at nearby Tulamben is one of the most dived sites in Asia.

  Candidasa   is an older resort town with reasonable infrastructure, a quieter and more faded feel, and low prices.

Both sit under Mount Agung, with the volcano dominating the skyline.

   The numbers

Land here is a fraction of the southern corridors and often below Tabanan. For the price of a small Canggu plot you buy something with a sea view and a volcano behind it.

That is genuine, and it is priced that way for reasons.

   The limitations

  Rental demand is thin and seasonal.   Divers come for a few nights within a wider trip. There is no equivalent of Canggu's month long villa market.

  The drive   is roughly two to two and a half hours from the airport.

  Amenities   are limited. No international schools, basic medical, few restaurants outside the small resorts.

  Resale is very shallow.   The pool of buyers who want the east coast and can lawfully purchase is small.

   Volcanic risk

Mount Agung is active. The 2017 and 2018 eruptions triggered evacuations within the exclusion zone and repeatedly closed the airport, which stopped tourism to the whole island.

Check the exclusion zones for the specific location and how insurance treats it.

   Who it suits

Buyers wanting a home, a dive base or a small boutique operation, with a long horizon and no need for liquidity or income.

Not buyers modelling yield, and not anyone who may need to sell within five years.

   Common questions

    Is Amed a good place to buy in Bali?
For price, quiet and diving, yes. For rental yield and resale liquidity, it is among the weakest areas on the island.

    How far is Amed from the airport?
Roughly two to two and a half hours, longer in heavy traffic or rain.

t: How do you plan an exit from Bali property?
s: Your buyer pool is decided on the day you purchase, not the day you list. Almost nobody models this and it is where returns are actually realised.
b:
Everyone models the entry. The exit is where the return is actually realised, and it is set by decisions made at purchase.

   Who can buy this from you?

  What you hold   Your future buyer  
             
  Leasehold, long term remaining   Foreigners. The pool shrinks as the term runs  
  Leasehold, short term remaining   Almost nobody  
  Hak Pakai   Foreigners with residency meeting the value threshold  
  HGB in a PT PMA   Buyers willing to take on a company, or buy its shares  
  Freehold via nominee   Nobody safely  

This is the single most important thing you decide at purchase and the one least considered.

   The four things that shrink your buyer pool

  A short remaining term.   Value decays non linearly. Eight years left trades far below half of thirty, because your buyer inherits the expiry.

  A weak extension clause.   "Market rate" is the landowner's option, and a sophisticated buyer prices it as a defect.

  Missing PBG or SLF.   Affects insurance, financing, licensing and resale simultaneously.

  A licence that does not transfer.   Removes the income that justifies your price.

   The cash market problem

Foreigners cannot realistically get local financing, so your buyer must have cash. That thins the pool permanently and makes pricing less forgiving.

It also means distress does not show up as forced sales, so price discovery is slow and asking prices drift above transacted levels.

   What to do a year before selling

  Get certificate, PBG, SLF and licence documents verified and in order
  Bring PT PMA filings fully current if a company holds it
  Do the refurbishment if it is due, because buyers discount more than it costs
  Assemble twelve months of clean operating statements
  Establish realistic transacted prices on your street, not asking prices

   Selling the company instead of the asset

Where a PT PMA holds the property, selling shares transfers the company, its licences and its history. It can be faster and cleaner for a buyer, part

t: Can you study in Indonesia on a student visa?
s: Sponsored by the institution, not by you, and it does not permit work. The language-school route is the one foreigners in Bali actually use.
b:
The student route exists and is more relevant to Bali than people realise, because language schools use it.

   How it works

The   institution sponsors you  . You do not apply independently. That means the school, university or training provider must be recognised and willing to act as sponsor.

A legitimate institution will have done this before and will know exactly what it needs from you.

   What it permits

Study at the sponsoring institution. Residence for the duration of the course.

  Not work.   A student permit does not grant the right to earn, and the enforcement test applied since April 2026 is activity rather than payment. Teaching a class on the side, taking freelance work, or running anything commercial is a violation.

   The Bahasa Indonesia route

The practical version for many foreigners in Bali is enrolling at a recognised language school. It provides a lawful basis to be here while you learn the language, which is genuinely useful.

Bahasa Indonesia is among the easier languages for English speakers: no tenses in the European sense, no gender, no cases, no tones, and a phonetic Latin alphabet. Useful conversational level is achievable in months.

   What to verify before enrolling

  Is the institution recognised and able to sponsor?
  Have they sponsored foreign students recently, and can they say so specifically?
  What is the attendance requirement, and is it enforced?
  What happens to the permit if you stop attending?
  Does the sponsorship cover the full period you intend to stay?

That attendance point matters. A permit granted for study and not used for study is a permit resting on a basis that no longer holds.

   What it does not lead to

The student route is not a path to permanent stay in the way consecutive years on a work or investor KITAS can be. Treat it as a lawful way to be here for a defined purpose rather than a long term residence strategy.

   Common questions

    Can foreigners study in Indonesia?
Yes, on a student permi

t: Is Echo Beach a good place to buy?
s: The northern end of Canggu, surf-led rather than cafe-led, slightly cheaper and with a different guest entirely.
b:
Echo Beach sits at the northern end of Canggu where the coast turns toward Pererenan, built around a reef break rather than a cafe strip.

   How it differs from Batu Bolong

Batu Bolong is walkable, dense and cafe driven. Echo Beach is surf driven, more spread out, and slightly cheaper per are for the same distance to sand.

The guest profile follows. Echo attracts surfers and people who want the beach without the crowd at the coffee shop. Batu Bolong attracts everyone else.

   The investment position

  Factor   Echo Beach  
             
  Entry price   Below Batu Bolong, above Pererenan  
  Rental demand   Strong, surf weighted  
  Seasonality   More pronounced, follows swell and dry season  
  Walkability   Moderate. Beach yes, amenities less so  
  Competing supply   Heavy, and building  
  Resale   Good, inside the Canggu buyer pool  

   What to check

  Exact walking distance to the sand, which varies sharply lane by lane
  Remaining lease term and the extension clause, since much stock is leasehold
  PBG and SLF, and whether extensions were approved
  Drainage. The lower lanes take water in wet season
  How many comparable villas are under construction within 500 metres
  The route out at 6pm, which is the same bottleneck as the rest of Canggu

   The honest read

Echo Beach gives you Canggu demand at a small discount to the walkable centre, with a guest who cares more about the wave than the flat white.

The oversupply problem that affects the whole corridor affects here too. A generic three bedroom pool villa competes on price. Something with a genuine outlook, an unusual size, or a short walk to the break does not.

   The northern edge

Where Echo Beach runs into Pererenan the character changes quickly: fewer cafes, more construction, wider plots and lower prices. That boundary has moved north repeatedly over the last five years and it will move again.
